newsitem.title: UK: Petronas $1.0 billion benchmark bond due next week.
newsitem.headline: Petronas $1.0 billion benchmark bond due next week.

text.p: Petroliam Nasional (Petronas) is expected to launch a $1.0 billion global bond late next week setting a benchmark for both Malaysian credits and the Asian region, new issues dealers said on Wednesday.
Petronas -- Malaysia's national oil company -- was likely to issue the bonds in two tranches with five- and 10-year maturities.
"(The Petronas deal) will be a benchmark for the borrower and the region. It will put the whole region into a positive light," a syndicate manager close to the deal said.
"As from next week we'll look at all markets seriously and decide what to do. We're likely to launch it then," he added.
CS First Boston and Salomon Brothers are joint lead managers for the transaction.
Petronas officials have already held investor presentations in Asia and are currently on roadshows in the U.S. They will also visit Frankfurt, London, Paris and Zurich.
Standard & Poor's today assigned its A-plus long term foreign currency rating to Petronas's proposed $1.0 billion global bond, in line with Malaysia's sovereign rating.
Dealers said although this was lower than Korea's AA-minus rating from S&P, the Petronas deal was likely to be priced in line with outstanding Korean bonds.

"Five-year Korean paper trades in the low 40's (basis points over U.S. Treasury notes) while 10-year paper trades in the high 50's. Although Korea has a better rating, Petronas is one of the strongest corporates of the region by a mile," an emerging markets trader said.
Petronas launched a $1.0 billion 10-year Yankee bond in 1995 which was now trading at 58 b.p. over U.S. Treasuries, dealers said. Its $500 million 2003 bond was trading at 48 b.p. over.
It also issued two samurai bonds totalling 22 billion yen in May this year.
S&P said Petronas would use the proceeds from the bond issue to refinance existing foreign currency borrowings and to finance part of the capital expenditure related to new projects.
"The rating on Petronas is based on its importance to the national economy, key strategic role, and strong operational and financial profile," S&P said, adding the outlook was positive.
"The outlook is consistent with the positive outlook of Malaysia and the prospect that Petronas will continue to play a vital role in the country's development."

Petronas president Hassan Marican has said the bond would be launched after the roadshow. He said it would be a global issue and the maturity and the amount would depend on the response from potential investors.
Petronas is wholly owned by the Malaysian government. Petronas Dagang Bhd is the listed retail arm.
On Tuesday, Petronas repeated it was not interested in buying a stake in Indonesia's PT Chandra Asri Petrochemical Centre.
In June, Petronas bought a 30 percent stake in South Africa's energy company Engen Ltd -- Malaysia's largest investment in South Africa thus far.
